nodes.summary: The Fibonacci parameters are the Lucas sequence parameters $P = 1$ and $Q = -1$; they satisfy the required condition $Q \ne 0$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci parameters for Lucas sequences

nodes.summary: If $(u_n)_{n \ge 0}$ is the Lucas sequence of the first kind with integer parameters $P$ and $Q$, then $u_1 = 1$.
nodes.title: Lucas sequence of the first kind: value at one

nodes.summary: If $(u_n)_{n \ge 0}$ is the Lucas sequence of the first kind with integer parameters $P$ and $Q$, then $u_0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Lucas sequence of the first kind: value at zero

nodes.summary: Lucas sequence parameters $(P, Q)$ are coprime when there exist integers $x$ and $y$ with $xP + yQ = 1$.
nodes.title: Coprime Lucas sequence parameters

nodes.summary: For integers $P$ and $Q$, a sequence of integers $(u_n)_{n \ge 0}$ is the Lucas sequence of the first kind with parameters $P$ and $Q$ when $u_0 = 0$, $u_1 = 1$, and $u_{n+2} = P u_{n+1} - Q u_n$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Lucas sequence of the first kind

nodes.summary: For integers $P$ and $Q$ and a natural number $p$, $p$ is a special prime for the Lucas parameters $(P, Q)$ if and only if $p$ is prime and $p$ divides both $P$ and $Q$ in $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Special primes are the common prime divisors of the parameters

nodes.summary: For integers $P$ and $Q$, a natural number $p$ is a special prime for the Lucas parameters $(P, Q)$ if $p$ is prime and $p$ divides $\gcd(P, Q)$.
nodes.title: Special primes of a Lucas pair

nodes.summary: A pair of integers $(P, Q)$ is nondegenerate when $Q \ne 0$ and, for all complex numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with $\alpha + \beta = P$ and $\alpha \beta = Q$, the quotient $\alpha / \beta$ is not a root of unity. Such $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the two roots of $x^2 - P x + Q$, in either order.
nodes.title: Nondegenerate Lucas pair

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers with $Q \ne 0$, let $U_n = U_n(P, Q)$ and $V_n = V_n(P, Q)$ be the associated Lucas sequences, and let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be elements of a field $K$ with $\alpha + \beta = P$ and $\alpha \beta = Q$ in $K$. If $\alpha \ne \beta$, then for every natural number $n$, $U_n = (\alpha^n - \beta^n) / (\alpha - \beta)$ and $V_n = \alpha^n + \beta^n$ in $K$. If $\beta = \alpha$, then for every…
nodes.title: Binet formulas for Lucas sequences over any field

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers with $Q \ne 0$, let $U_n = U_n(P, Q)$ and $V_n = V_n(P, Q)$ be the associated Lucas sequences, and let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be elements of a field $K$ of characteristic zero with $\alpha + \beta = P$ and $\alpha \beta = Q$ in $K$. If $\alpha \ne \beta$, then for every natural number $n$, $U_n = (\alpha^n - \beta^n) / (\alpha - \beta)$ and $V_n = \alpha^n + \beta^n$ in $K$. If…
nodes.title: Binet formulas for Lucas sequences

nodes.summary: The Lucas numbers are the natural numbers $L_n$ defined by $L_0 = 2$, $L_1 = 1$ and $L_{n+2} = L_{n+1} + L_n$ for every natural number $n$. They begin $2, 1, 3, 4, 7, \dots$.
nodes.title: Lucas numbers

nodes.summary: Lucas sequence parameters are a pair of integers $(P, Q)$ with $Q \ne 0$.
nodes.title: Parameters of a Lucas sequence

nodes.summary: For Lucas sequence parameters $(P, Q)$ and every natural number $n$, the Lucas sequence $U = U(P, Q)$ satisfies $U_{n+2} = P U_{n+1} - Q U_n$.
nodes.title: Recurrence for the Lucas sequence $U(P, Q)$

nodes.summary: For Lucas sequence parameters $(P, Q)$ and every natural number $n$, the Lucas sequence $U = U(P, Q)$ satisfies $U_{n+1}^2 - U_n U_{n+2} = Q^n$.
nodes.title: Cassini's identity for Lucas sequences

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the $n$-th term of the Lucas sequence $U(1, -1)$ equals the Fibonacci number $F_n$, where $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$ and $F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n$.
nodes.title: The Lucas sequence $U(1, -1)$ is the Fibonacci sequence

nodes.summary: For Lucas sequence parameters $(P, Q)$, the Lucas sequence $U(P, Q)$ is the integer sequence $(U_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = P U_{n+1} - Q U_n$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Lucas sequence $U(P, Q)$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the $n$-th term of the companion Lucas sequence $V(1, -1)$ equals the $n$-th Lucas number $L_n$.
nodes.title: The Lucas sequence $V(1, -1)$ gives the Lucas numbers

nodes.summary: For Lucas sequence parameters $(P, Q)$, the companion Lucas sequence $V(P, Q)$ is the integer sequence $(V_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $V_0 = 2$, $V_1 = P$ and $V_{n+2} = P V_{n+1} - Q V_n$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Companion Lucas sequence $V(P, Q)$

nodes.summary: If $(u_n)_{n \ge 0}$ is the Lucas sequence of the first kind with integer parameters $P$ and $Q$, then $u_{n+2} = P u_{n+1} - Q u_n$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Lucas sequence of the first kind: the recurrence

nodes.summary: For all integers $P$ and $Q$ with $Q \neq 0$ and all natural numbers $m$ and $n$, the Lucas sequences $U_n = U_n(P, Q)$ and $V_n = V_n(P, Q)$ satisfy $2U_{m+n} = U_m V_n + V_m U_n$.
nodes.title: Addition formula $2U_{m+n} = U_m V_n + V_m U_n$ for Lucas sequences

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
